relationships.subject: M1 macrophages
relationships.evidence_quote: TNF-α is released by M1 macrophages during acute inflammation and is responsible for various intracellular signaling events leading to abnormal cell death (39).

relationships.subject: M1 macrophages
relationships.evidence_quote: In a co-culture experiment of M1 macrophages and NPCs in vitro, M1 macrophages activated the HMGB1/Myd88/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3, resulting in increased IL-1β release (48).

relationships.subject: TNF-α
relationships.evidence_quote: TNF-α can also activate the NF-κB and p38-MAPK signaling pathways in NPCs, induce CCL4 expression, and further promote M1 macrophage infiltration (44).

key_findings: Review: M1 macrophages drive NP matrix catabolism via TNF-α and IL-1β, M2 promote repair
